rounds.text: JTL Industries Ltd trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.89x against a sector benchmark of 4.69x, while its EV/EBITDA of 17.59x also sits slightly below its sector benchmark [E7, E11]. The underlying fundamental growth is exceptional over longer time horizons, anchored by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 34% and an extraordinary 10-year compounded profit growth rate of 81% [E14, E18]. Recent performance confirms strong operational momentum, evidenced by a quarterly operating margin expansion to 8% in March 2026 compared to 4% in the year-ago quarter, alongside a 53% year-on-year surge in net profit [E31, E65]. The company remains conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x, while capital expenditure is aggressively ramping up through a 144.4% increase in capital-work-in-progress to reach Rs 154 Cr [E38, E40]. Institutional participation is showing positive expansion, reflected by foreign institutions increasing their stake and overall institutional money flow reading positive [E42, E44]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation models place the share's value above the current market price of ₹ 73.9, offering a concrete margin of safety [E2, E45, E46]. Conceded: [E34], [E36], [E62].

JTL Industries Ltd trades at an expensive P/E of 32.2x [E1] despite generating low returns, with a trailing ROE of 7.0% [E13] and an ROCE of 8.46% [E10] that significantly lag sector benchmarks of 15.3% [E9] and 18.2% [E10]. Growth has stalled dramatically over the medium term, evidenced by negative trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of -6% [E17], a -1% decline in compounded profit over three years [E20], and a further -10% drop in profit over the trailing twelve months [E21]. Cash generation has collapsed into negative territory, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -10 Cr [E35], a free cash flow of Rs -131 Cr [E36], and a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.11x in March 2026 [E34]. Meanwhile, financial risk is escalating as borrowings surged nearly fourfold to Rs 203 Cr from Rs 53 Cr a year earlier [E39], coinciding with a reduction in promoter shareholding by 6.52 percentage points down to 49.26% [E41]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong long-term historical compounding with 10-year sales and profit growth at 34% and 81% respectively [E14, E18], alongside an institutional money flow showing positive accumulation of +1.58 percentage points [E44].

Conceded: trailing ROE is 7.0% [E13] and ROCE is 8.46% [E10]. However, the market price of ₹ 73.9 [E2] is visibly under-appreciated when evaluated against a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 94, offering a margin of safety of 21.2% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price only prices in 14.7% earnings growth, which is below the 18.0% base case assumption [E47]. Although trailing twelve-month profit growth declined by 10% [E21], recent quarterly performance reveals a sharp turnaround with net profit surging 53% year-on-year [E65], alongside a quarterly operating margin expansion of 4 percentage points to 8% [E31]. Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -10 Cr [E35], but this coincides with a massive capital expenditure push as Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) surged by 144.4% to reach Rs 154 Cr in March 2026 [E40]. Finally, the surging borrowings to Rs 203 Cr [E39] are comfortably supported by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.16x [E38], while institutional money flows remain positive with a holding increase of 1.58 percentage points [E44].

Conceded: intrinsic value stands at ₹ 94 [E45] and quarterly net profit surged 53% year-on-year [E65]. However, relying on a reverse DCF implying 14.7% growth ignores that the trailing twelve-month profit growth actually contracted by 10% [E21], and 3-year profit growth sits at -1% [E20]. While the bull points to a sharp operating margin expansion in the latest quarter [E31], the yearly operating-margin trend is explicitly rated as inconsistent over the last 2 years [E32]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio remains conservative at 0.16x [E38], but borrowings jumped sharply to ₹ 203 Cr from ₹ 53 Cr a year earlier [E39], coinciding with negative operating cash flow of ₹ -10 Cr [E35] and a severe free cash flow burn of ₹ -131 Cr [E36]. Furthermore, promoter holding has eroded by 6.52 percentage points down to 49.26% [E41], signaling insider divestment during this very capital-expenditure push.
